summary: Creating the app and distributing it publicly is self-serve, but new commercially distributed apps that are not in the Slack Marketplace get a 1 request/minute limit on message-history methods. Marketplace review is optional on paper and nearly required if you read history.
time_to_production: Unlisted public distribution: self-serve, no review. Marketplace: up to 10 business days preliminary feedback plus up to 10 weeks functional review (new apps), not expeditable.
effort: Own workspace: small. Public distribution: checklist and HTTPS. Marketplace: landing, support and privacy pages, test accounts with dummy data, demo video, 10 active workspaces.

approval.kind: Two layers: (1) workspace admin approval only where 'Require approved apps' is on; (2) optional Slack Marketplace review. Public distribution itself is not reviewed.
approval.who_reviews: Workspace Owners / app managers; Slack Marketplace team
approval.stated_wait: Marketplace: up to 10 business days preliminary, up to 10 weeks functional (new), up to 6 weeks (resubmission). Admin approval: no official figure.

steps.title: Create a Slack app
steps.detail: Create at api.slack.com/apps; client ID and client secret appear on the App Management page.

steps.title: Choose minimal bot scopes (scope) and user scopes (user_scope)
steps.detail: Bot and user scope sets must be requested in separate OAuth flows per doc; scopes accumulate across installs, removal requires revoking the token.

steps.title: Configure HTTPS Redirect URL under OAuth & Permissions
steps.detail: Must be HTTPS, no '#' anchor; redirect_uri must match or be subpath of a configured URL; same value in authorize and access steps if multiple configured, else bad_redirect_uri.

steps.title: Implement authorize redirect + code exchange at oauth.v2.access
steps.detail: Redirect user to Slack authorize endpoint, receive temporary code at redirect_uri, exchange with client secret for access token.

steps.title: Install into own workspace
steps.detail: Installing needs a user with permission; if the workspace requires approved apps, an Owner/app manager must approve.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution (for other workspaces)
steps.detail: App dashboard > Manage Distribution > complete checklist > Activate Public Distribution. Requires SSL on redirect/request URLs and OAuth 2.0 flow. Yields Add to Slack button and install URL. Not reviewed.

steps.title: Optional: submit to Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Submit from app config; automated tests, test accounts with dummy data, demo video; preliminary then functional review. Needs >=10 active workspaces (used within 28 days).

requirements.text: HTTPS redirect URL configured under OAuth & Permissions (no '#' anchor).
Bot scopes and user scopes are requested in separate OAuth flows.
Marketplace: at least 10 active workspaces, per-scope justification, signing secrets (not verification tokens), TLS 1.2+, OAuth state parameter.

composio.note: Composio can supply the OAuth app so you can start without registering one; users see 'Composio' on the consent screen, scopes are Composio's defaults, and rate-limit quota is shared. Register your own app (this guide) for production branding, custom scopes, a dedicated quota, faster polling, or private instances.

gotchas.text: Since 2025-05-29, commercially distributed apps not in the Marketplace, created on/after that date or newly installed, get Tier 1 on conversations.history and conversations.replies: 1 request/minute, max/default limit param 15. Marketplace apps, existing installs of older unlisted apps, and internal customer-built apps (50+/min, 1000 objects) are unaffected.
Marketplace requires >=10 active workspaces installed, yet unlisted public distribution is rate-limited; a chicken-and-egg for read-history apps.
Bot and user scopes need separate OAuth flows; Sign in with Slack scopes cannot be combined.
Scopes accumulate; removing one requires revoking the whole token.
Once published to Marketplace, distribution cannot be toggled off; must discontinue listing. Deactivating public distribution removes the app from other workspaces.

Marketplace submission: Slack workspace credentials not accepted as test accounts; apps using only Sign in with Slack or only an MCP server are excluded; use signing secrets not verification tokens; use OAuth state param; TLS 1.2+.
Published Marketplace app is locked; new scopes/features require resubmission and staging app; installing with unreviewed scopes causes customer errors.

blockers.blocker: New unlisted commercially distributed apps are throttled to 1 request/minute (limit 15) on conversations.history and conversations.replies.
blockers.what_to_do: Get Marketplace approval, build as an internal customer-built app per workspace (unaffected), or try the Events API instead of polling (inferred, not stated in docs).

blockers.blocker: Marketplace needs 10 active workspaces but unlisted distribution is throttled (inferred chicken-and-egg).
blockers.what_to_do: Bootstrap through pilot installs via unlisted public distribution; Slack's docs describe it as suited to pilots.
An Owner or appointed app manager approves; ask for the minimum scopes since admins weigh them.
